name: Fraud — instant-payments / real-time-rails risk (FedNow, UPI, SEPA Instant, RTP)
category: Currently-stated (README) target, expanded — fraud detection on real-time rails
parent_research_topic: Beava use cases — current and potential applications of beava as a real-time feature server

domain_fit.domain_name: Instant-payments / real-time-rails fraud and AML decisioning
domain_fit.one_line_definition: An issuing or beneficiary bank (or its fraud/AML engine) must decide within a single-digit-second SLA whether to release, hold, or reject an irrevocable real-time credit transfer on FedNow, RTP, SEPA Instant or UPI before the payment is irreversibly settled.
domain_fit.representative_jobs_to_be_done: 1) Score every outbound instant-payment submission for APP-fraud (authorized-push-payment), business-email-compromise, and account-takeover risk inside the rail's end-to-end time budget (10s SEPA Inst, ~20s FedNow/RTP, ~15s UPI request/response after NPCI's June 2025 change). 2) Apply per-account-pair velocity, distinct-counterparty and first-seen-payee checks before the credit is released, plus mule-receipt anomaly detection on the beneficiary side (sudden inbound spikes, fan-in/fan-out, dormant-account-wakes). 3) Maintain real-time velocity counters so a customer-screening / pre-payment 'network intelligence' / Verification-of-Payee lookup can be combined with behavioural and amount-based features into a single sub-100 ms decision.
domain_fit.event_shapes: ISO 20022 pacs.008 (FIToFICstmrCdtTrf) submission, pacs.002 status, camt.054 credit notification, plus producer-side events: login_attempt, device_bind, beneficiary_added, payment_initiated, payment_authorised, payment_completed, scam_reported. Key fields: debtor_account, creditor_account, debtor_agent_BIC, creditor_agent_BIC, amount, currency, channel (mobile/web/API), device_id, ip, geolocation, session_id, beneficiary_first_seen_ts, purpose_code, end_to_end_id. For UPI: VPA (handle@bank), psp_app_id, mobile_imei, sim, upi_ref. For APP-fraud signals: time_since_payee_added, intervention_warning_shown, customer_typed_amount_changes.
domain_fit.feature_shapes: Counters: count(payments) per (debtor_account, window=1m/5m/1h/24h), count(distinct creditor_account) per debtor in 24h, sum(amount) per (debtor, window). Velocities: payments-per-minute per device, per IP, per (debtor+channel). Distances/impossible-travel: geohash/H3 distance from last login to payment-initiation, time-vs-distance over last N events. Distributions: amount z-score vs debtor's 30-day distribution, time-of-day percentile per account, hour-of-week histogram. First-seen flags: is_first_payment_to_creditor, time_since_beneficiary_added (<24h is a strong APP-scam signal). Beneficiary-side: fan-in count (n distinct senders to creditor in 1h/24h), credit_burst (sum-in / 30d-baseline), dormant_wake (days_since_last_activity > 90 AND sum_in_1h > threshold). Mostly tumbling 1m/5m/1h plus sliding 24h/7d/30d; HLL acceptable for distinct-counterparty cardinality.
domain_fit.entity_grain: Primary keys overlap and are typically tracked in parallel: (debtor_account), (creditor_account), (debtor_account + creditor_account pair), (device_id), (IP / ASN), (session_id), (BIC / participant), and for UPI (VPA, IMEI, sim). The (debtor+creditor) pair is the critical APP-fraud grain — it's where first-seen and pair-velocity features live.
domain_fit.window_semantics_required: Mixed. Pre-execution decisioning needs short tumbling/sliding windows (1s, 10s, 1m, 5m, 1h) computed exactly because they drive a release-vs-reject decision on an irrevocable transfer. Longer-horizon profiling (30d, 90d distribution baselines, behavioural baselines) can tolerate approximate sketches (HLL for distinct-counterparty count, CMS for heavy hitters, t-digest for amount quantiles). Session windows are useful on the originating channel (mobile-app session → payment) but the financial event is point-in-time at submission.
domain_fit.exactly_once_or_idempotency_needs: Strict idempotency required. Same pacs.008 / end_to_end_id replayed must not double-count velocity; AML/regulator audits demand reproducible feature values at decision time. At-least-once delivery from upstream rails is the norm, so the feature server must dedupe on (end_to_end_id, message_id) or be exposed an idempotency token.

technical_fit.latency_budget: Feature read p99 < 10 ms; full scoring pipeline (features + model + rules + Verification-of-Payee + sanctions cache check) typically budgeted at 50–200 ms end-to-end so the bank still has headroom inside the 10 s rail SLA. SEPA Instant rulebook breaks the 10 s into ~5 s originator-PSP, 7 s CSM, 9 s end-to-end.
technical_fit.feature_freshness_sla: Features driving the live decision must reflect the current event itself — i.e. the just-arrived submission must update counters before scoring or atomically as part of the get-and-update. Effective freshness target: 0 ms (same-event). Profiling/baseline features can tolerate seconds-to-minutes staleness.
technical_fit.throughput_profile: Steady-state per buyer varies widely. A mid-tier US bank on FedNow/RTP today sees thousands of EPS (RTP network-wide hit ~1.8M daily transactions / ~20 TPS network average in Oct 2025, but a single large bank may see hundreds of EPS with spikes into low thousands). SEPA Instant peaks are higher — many EU PSPs already process hundreds to low thousands of EPS post-Oct 2025 mandate. UPI is the extreme case: NPCI processed ~7,500 TPS average in Aug 2025 across the whole switch; a top issuer/PSP can see 500–1,500 EPS sustained. beava's published ~684k EPS single-M4-core (TCP+msgpack+parallel=16) is comfortably above any single-tenant requirement and gives headroom for the 20–100 feature lookups per decision. [uncertain] — exact per-bank EPS is not publicly disclosed for most institutions.
technical_fit.read_to_write_ratio: Roughly balanced to slightly read-heavy. Every payment event is one write (counter update) and 20–100+ feature reads for the scoring model, so reads dominate by ~30–100x.
technical_fit.state_size_estimate: For a top-tier US bank: ~50–200M accounts × ~5–20 KB of per-entity feature state (counters across many windows, distinct-counterparty HLL, amount sketches, beneficiary first-seen map) ≈ 0.25–4 TB hot working set. Counterparty-pair grain explodes this — (debtor × creditor) pairs can be 10–100x the account count, but most pairs are inactive and amenable to TTL eviction. For an EU PSP or UPI PSP the entity count is similar (UPI: 350M+ users). beava's in-memory-only model fits a single mid-tier bank's hot set on a beefy node, but a top-tier US/EU/Indian rails participant will need sharding for the full footprint. [uncertain] — bytes/entity is a planning estimate, not measured.
technical_fit.cardinality_pattern: Mixed. Account-level entities (debtor, creditor) grow slowly with onboarding. Pair-level (debtor+creditor) is explosive in the long tail but bounded for any given debtor (most consumers transact with <100 distinct payees / month). Device and IP cardinality is explosive and unbounded — needs HLL / sketches and aggressive TTL. APP-fraud beneficiaries are usually fresh accounts (first-seen=true) so 'new creditor' is itself a feature.
technical_fit.typical_state_lifecycle_and_ttl: Short-window counters (1s–1h): seconds to hours TTL. Behavioural baselines: 30–90 days rolling. Mule-detection signals: 45 days is the published heuristic (NICE Actimize: majority of mule accounts exhibit mule behaviour within 45 days of opening). Regulator-grade retention of features used at decision time: 5–7 years for AML/BSA, but the live serving store only needs to hold the working set; the 7-year retention is satisfied by archiving the decision log, not by keeping it hot in beava.
technical_fit.typical_feature_count_per_decision: 20–200+ per payment. Stripe-style production scorers use hundreds of features per inference; FedNow/SEPA Instant deployments report ensemble models combining behavioural biometrics, device intelligence, network/graph signals, and transaction history — the model side reads dozens-to-hundreds of features in a single batch_get.
technical_fit.durability_requirements: Regulator-grade. AML/BSA, FFIEC, PSD3/SCA, EU IPR (Instant Payments Regulation) all expect the bank to reproduce the feature values used for a declined or reported transaction. beava's WAL + periodic snapshot story covers crash-safety, but the feature server itself is not the system-of-record — the rail's pacs.008 archive is. beava feature state can be treated as recomputable from the WAL of inbound events, which is acceptable to most regulators provided the upstream event log is durable. The 'refuse on network-FS' guardrail is the right default for this domain — silent fsync lies on NFS would compromise crash recovery.
technical_fit.deployment_topology_fit: Single-binary-per-region is the natural v0 fit (one beava per data centre per bank). For a top-tier issuer or an EU PSP that must serve cross-border SEPA Instant, multi-region active-active is desirable but not strictly required since each rail leg is region-local. Sidecar to the bank's existing scoring engine (Feedzai, Featurespace, NICE Actimize, in-house) is a realistic adoption path. beava's lack of in-process sharding in v0 caps single-tenant scale at one node's RAM, which is fine for a mid-tier bank or an EU neobank but not for a top-tier US/Indian rails participant.

commercial_fit.who_buys: Fraud / financial-crime engineering teams inside banks, credit unions, and payment-service providers; ML-platform teams at fintechs running their own scoring; vendors of fraud platforms (Feedzai, Featurespace, NICE Actimize, ACI, Hawk.AI, Flagright, ComplyAdvantage) who embed a feature-serving layer; and regtech/AML startups serving SEPA Instant PSPs that need a new low-latency stack to meet the Oct-2025 mandate.
commercial_fit.market_size_signal: Large and regulator-pulled. Global fraud-detection-in-banking market is forecast in the multi-$10B range (Research and Markets 2024–2029 report names ACI, Featurespace, Feedzai, Fiserv, Fraudio, SEON, TransUnion as the competitor leaderboard). UK APP-fraud losses alone were £459.7M across ~250k cases in 2023; the Oct 2024 PSR mandatory-reimbursement regime (up to £85k per claim, 50:50 between sending and receiving PSP) put direct P&L pressure on every UK PSP. UPI fraud in FY24–25 was reported at 6.32 lakh cases / ₹485 crore (with broader estimates >13 lakh cases and >₹1,000 crore losses). FedNow's $10M limit lift (effective Nov 2025, not Nov 2024 as commonly cited) transforms RTP/FedNow from retail-convenience into corporate-treasury rails and re-opens fraud RFPs at every participant bank.
commercial_fit.urgency_drivers: 1) SEPA Instant mandatory acceptance (Jan 2025) and sending (Oct 2025) across the eurozone — every EU PSP must do AML, sanctions and fraud inside 10 s. 2) EU Verification of Payee mandate (9 Oct 2025 for euro states, 9 Jul 2027 for non-euro). 3) UK PSR mandatory APP-fraud reimbursement (live 7 Oct 2024). 4) FedNow $10M limit (Nov 2025) and RTP $10M limit (Feb 2025) — both push high-value-payment fraud into real-time decisioning. 5) US AFP 2025 Payments Fraud Survey: 63% of firms saw check fraud in 2024 vs. 2% on RTP/FedNow — fraud is migrating, regulators expect controls to follow. 6) NPCI cut UPI request/response from 30s to 15s in June 2025, shrinking the decision budget further.
commercial_fit.regulatory_or_audit_constraints: AML/BSA (US), FFIEC retail-payments guidance, EU Instant Payments Regulation (IPR) and EU AMLR, PSD3/SCA, UK PSR APP-reimbursement rules, RBI/NPCI directions for UPI, FinCEN SAR reporting, OFAC/EU sanctions screening. Note the EU IPR Art. 5d shift: PSPs must screen their full customer base against EU sanctions lists daily and on every list update, rather than per-transaction during the 10-second window — this changes what features the scoring path needs to see (a precomputed 'is_sanctioned' flag rather than an inline screen). Data-protection layer: GDPR for EU, DPDP Act for India, CCPA for US. PCI-DSS applies if card data is co-resident.
commercial_fit.time_to_value_signal: 1–2 weeks for a velocity-and-impossible-travel demo against synthetic pacs.008 traffic. 1–2 months for a shadow-mode deployment alongside an incumbent scoring engine. 3–6+ months for a regulator-grade production cutover (model validation, SOX/SOC2/audit, runbook for WAL/snapshot recovery, sign-off on the in-memory durability model).

competition.incumbents: Generic streaming and feature-store stacks deployed for this use case today: Redis (Enterprise/Cluster) used as a real-time feature store at scale — one major card network publicly cited running ~700k TPS of scoring on Redis; Apache Flink for stateful stream processing (rolling aggregates, session windows, enrichment); Aerospike for sub-ms real-time payments feature serving (Aerospike has explicit payments-fraud collateral); Tecton, Feast, Hopsworks, Chalk, Fennel as ML feature stores; Materialize and RisingWave as streaming SQL stores; ksqlDB and Kafka Streams on the Kafka side. The dominant pattern is 'Kafka + Flink + Redis-or-Aerospike + scoring engine', which beava collapses into a single binary.
competition.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Domain-specific fraud platforms — Feedzai (processes ~$8B/yr, protects ~1B consumers), Featurespace ARIC (now Visa-owned; protects ~500M consumers, processes ~100B payments/yr), NICE Actimize, ACI Worldwide (ReD/Proactive Risk Manager), SAS Fraud Management, IBM Safer Payments, Verafin (Nasdaq) — all of these include built-in feature engines. AML-side: ComplyAdvantage, Hawk.AI, Flagright, AMLYZE, Castellum.AI, Sumsub, Sardine. Behavioural biometrics / device side: BioCatch, ThreatMark, Incognia, LexisNexis Risk Solutions. Graph/network: Linkurious, TigerGraph, Neo4j. beava would typically slot underneath one of these as the real-time feature layer rather than replace the full platform — except for in-house builds at large banks.
competition.beava_differentiator: 1) Single binary, no Kafka+Flink+Redis sprawl — credible 'Redis-for-stateful-features with 50+ aggregation primitives' positioning. 2) ~684k EPS on a single core gives multi-x headroom over today's per-bank rails throughput, so a single node serves a real bank. 3) Native velocity / distance / distribution / rate primitives mean an engineer declares `@bv.table(key=...)` instead of writing Flink jobs and Redis Lua scripts. 4) HTTP/JSON + framed TCP (JSON / msgpack) means the bank's existing scoring engine (Python XGBoost, Java rules, ONNX) can call beava directly from the decision path. 5) Apache-2.0, no open-core — critical for regulated buyers who reject mixed-licence stacks and for fraud-platform vendors who want to embed beava without licence friction. 6) Atomic per-event update-and-read fits the 'feature value at decision time must reflect this event' requirement that pure cache-of-precomputed-features stacks struggle with.
competition.where_beava_loses_today: 1) No TLS — disqualifying for any production bank deployment without an in-front reverse proxy, and even then most fraud teams want mTLS to the feature server. 2) No authn/authz — every regulated buyer needs RBAC at minimum. 3) No in-process sharding — caps single-tenant scale at one node, which is a hard limit for top-tier US/EU/Indian rails participants. 4) In-memory-only with WAL+snapshot — most fraud teams are nervous about losing 30–90 days of behavioural baselines on a crash even with WAL replay; they want point-in-time recovery and tiered storage of cold features. 5) No triggers / no event-driven actions — fraud teams want 'if velocity > N in 5m, emit step-up-auth event' baked in. 6) No native sanctions-list/PEP-list join — every competitor ships this. 7) No graph features for mule-ring detection — Linkurious/TigerGraph/Neo4j cover this gap today. 8) No multi-tenancy — a fraud-platform vendor wanting to embed beava would need either per-tenant binaries or a sharding/namespace story.
competition.integration_surface: Banks use Kafka or vendor-specific message buses upstream of the scoring engine; pacs.008/pacs.002 enter via SWIFT, FedLine, Fed FedNow API, RTP API, EBA RT1 / TIPS / SEPA Instant CSMs, or NPCI UPI Switch. beava's HTTP-and-TCP-push model is unusual in this stack — most feature stores are Kafka-consumer-shaped (Tecton, Feast, Hopsworks, Fennel) and expect a streaming source. The right beava integration is either (a) a thin Kafka-to-beava-TCP sidecar, or (b) direct ingestion from the bank's payment processor / orchestration layer (which already speaks HTTP/REST in modern stacks). gRPC support would close a recognised gap with Tecton/Chalk.
competition.scoring_engine_coupling: Both. Buyers plug beava (or any feature store) into (a) an external rules engine (Drools, OpenRules, FEEL, Snowflake/dbt-based rules, or the rules engine inside Feedzai/Featurespace/NICE) and (b) one or more ML scorers (XGBoost, LightGBM, ONNX, TensorFlow Serving). Production fraud stacks always run rules and ML in parallel because regulators expect explainable rule paths.

adoption_signals.existing_public_users_or_case_studies: No public beava case study in this domain yet. Comparable platforms with named public users for this exact use case: Redis (top-3 card network at ~700k TPS scoring; multiple bank case studies on real-time fraud); Aerospike (PayPal, Barclays, others publicly cited for payments fraud); Tecton (Block/Square, Plaid, Coinbase publicly cited for fraud-style risk decisioning); Featurespace ARIC at HSBC, NatWest, Worldpay etc.; Feedzai at Citi, Standard Chartered, Lloyds. ThreatMark, Incognia, BioCatch all publish FedNow-readiness collateral. [uncertain] — exact named users vary; I have not independently verified each case study.
adoption_signals.community_discussions: [uncertain] — I did not surface any beava-specific Discord / GitHub Discussion / RFC threads on instant-payments fraud as of the search date. Broader community signal is strong: FedNow Explorer 'Fraud Control Tower' is an entire Fed-Reserve-hosted resource; PYMNTS, ABA Banking Journal, The Clearing House, NICE Actimize, Feedzai, Featurespace, Flagright, Castellum.AI, AMLYZE, Hawk.AI all publish weekly on this topic.
adoption_signals.examples_or_demos_in_repo: [uncertain] — the beava-use-cases/results directory exists but I could not locate an `examples/` directory in the repo at /tmp/docker-desktop-root/run/desktop/mnt/host/d/Code/Beava/beava during this research (find returned no results). If an instant-payments-fraud vertical demo exists today, its path was not visible from this agent's filesystem snapshot.
adoption_signals.adversarial_pressure_level: Maximum. This is the most actively adversarial domain in commercial computing alongside ad-fraud and anti-cheat. Adversaries iterate in hours, run mule-account farms, automate scams via social engineering kits, exploit every new rail within weeks of launch, and specifically target the rail's irreversibility. Feature drift is constant; models must retrain monthly or faster.

risk_and_non_goals.non_goals: 1) Historical batch backfill of 5-year transaction archives — that belongs in a warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks) and feeds beava via offline-to-online sync, not via beava itself. 2) Full event archive / system-of-record for the pacs.008 / camt.054 stream — the rail's own log and the bank's payment-orchestration layer are the SoR; beava holds derived features. 3) Cross-entity joins (e.g. 'all customers connected to mule-ring X') — that's a graph database job (TigerGraph, Neo4j, Linkurious), not a feature store. 4) Long-horizon AML investigation workflows / case management — Verafin, Hawk.AI, NICE Actimize own that. 5) Sanctions-list / PEP-list maintenance — buy from ComplyAdvantage, Castellum.AI, Refinitiv. 6) Model training and model registry — Vertex / SageMaker / MLflow territory.
risk_and_non_goals.open_engineering_gaps: To be production-grade for any regulated bank or PSP, beava would need, in roughly decreasing priority: (1) TLS termination (mTLS preferred) — non-negotiable; (2) Authn/authz — API tokens minimum, RBAC and per-tenant namespaces preferred, ideally OIDC/SAML for admin; (3) In-process sharding or a documented horizontal-scale story (consistent-hash router, replication, failover) so a top-tier issuer can run beava without a single-node ceiling; (4) Hot-replica / standby with synchronous WAL streaming so a node loss does not drop 30–90 day behavioural baselines; (5) Triggers / 'fire when counter crosses threshold' — fraud teams want step-up-auth and circuit-breaker events emitted by the feature server; (6) Per-feature TTL and tiered storage (RAM → local SSD) so 90-day baselines don't have to all live in RAM; (7) Secondary indexes for ad-hoc investigations ('show me all debtors with >5 distinct creditors in 1h'); (8) gRPC surface in addition to HTTP/TCP — Tecton/Chalk/Feast set this expectation; (9) Idempotency tokens on push (dedupe by end_to_end_id) — required for at-least-once upstream rails; (10) Audit log of every read (who-asked-what-when) for AML reproducibility; (11) Native sanctions-list / PEP-list join surface (or at minimum a cleanly documented external-lookup hook); (12) Multi-tenancy so fraud-platform vendors can embed beava on behalf of many bank customers; (13) Time-travel / 'as-of' reads so a regulator can ask 'what was the feature value at 14:32:07.123 yesterday?'; (14) Drift / monitoring exporters (Prometheus + OpenTelemetry).
risk_and_non_goals.trigger_action_required: Yes — fraud teams strongly prefer event-driven actions in addition to feature serving (emit a 'step-up-auth required' event when velocity > N in window W; emit 'hold for review' when sum(amount, 5m) > customer_baseline * K). beava today is feature-serving only, which means the caller's scoring engine has to do the polling-and-thresholding. Adding a trigger / webhook surface is a high-leverage feature for this domain.
